notes: TMax is by far the strongest corpus: it has a whole family of 'C/C++ crashes and leaks, fix it and pass Valgrind' tasks, and two (task_000583 optimization-only UB from a missing asm clobber; task_002407 -O2 UB + bad comparator) reproduce the exact release-only-crash-from-UB scenario of the TB task. TerminalWorld contributes genuine C++ crash-debugging (tw_7829 uninitialized-member segfault via GDB; tw_245032 openal-soft crash). RTS shortlist was almost entirely boilerplate (sqrt.cc build chores, 'print 599' multi-file C, ARM64 assembly starters) - discarded; the real RTS signal is the reproduce/diagnose-a-crash-under-GDB and heap/stack-overflow families I found by searching. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench cannot match domain (all Python) or task_form (issue-fix), so their scores are honestly low; the one real skill bridge is the *-initialization-order* bug class in SWE-Smith (starlette/faker/json-logger), which mirrors the static-initialization-order fiasco, and setuptools-4676's debug-vs-release-build reasoning in Rebench. Merge note: the buggy-png crash seed and the PHP #81698 segfault seed and the sudo CVE-2021-3156 seed each appear in BOTH RTS and TerminalWorld, so some picks across those two are siblings.
